review.why: Requires fresh verification evidence before any claim that work is done, fixed or passing, with a gate function and a table of what counts.
review.summary: Iron law: no completion claims without fresh verification evidence. The gate is identify the proving command, run it in full, read the output and exit code, verify, and only then claim. A table lists what each claim needs and what is not enough, red flags such as should, probably and early satisfaction, and a rationalization table. It includes not trusting agent success reports without a diff.
strengths: Maps each claim type to the evidence it requires
Treats subagent success reports as unverified until the diff is checked
Short enough to apply every time
cautions: Strict wording: some claims may be cheap to skip verifying
Later sections were not read in full
Needs runnable checks in the project
